subject: Eponyms
title: High-Yield Eponymous Nodes & Spots
preview: Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, Roth spots, Koplik spots and named metastatic nodules are useful pattern-recognition clues.

sections.title: Infective endocarditis signs
points: Osler nodes: classically tender nodules on distal digits.
Janeway lesions: classically painless lesions of palms or soles.
Roth spots: retinal hemorrhagic lesions with pale centers; they are not exclusive to endocarditis.

sections.title: Viral illness clue
points: Koplik spots are small whitish buccal mucosal lesions classically associated with measles.
Recognize the importance of infection-control precautions and clinical confirmation when measles is suspected.

sections.title: Named malignant associations
points: Virchow node: left supraclavicular lymphadenopathy may reflect thoracic or abdominal malignancy but has several possible causes.
Sister Mary Joseph nodule: an umbilical metastatic deposit can occur with intra-abdominal or pelvic malignancy.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Neither a missing skin sign nor a named node excludes the underlying disease.
Clinical signs should trigger targeted investigation rather than be treated as standalone diagnostic proof.

quickRevision: Painful Osler nodes and painless Janeway lesions are classically associated with infective endocarditis, but may be absent.
Koplik spots can appear with measles before the typical exanthem.
Virchow node and Sister Mary Joseph nodule can signal underlying malignancy and require proper diagnostic assessment.

quiz.question: Virchow node refers to which lymph node?
quiz.explanation: Virchow's Node: Enlarged, hard, non-tender left supraclavicular lymph node.
